Unanswered Questions What is the connection with Horne's Department Store? Why doesn't the One-Armed Man remember BOB? What is the significance of Hank's domino and the drawing of it he sent to Josie? CAST LIST EPISODES CHARACTERS

title: 5 - Cooper's Dreams | Twin Peaks
text: 5 - Cooper's Dreams | Twin Peaks ← Previous 5 - Cooper's Dreams Written by Mark Frost Directed by Lesli Linka Glatter Original Airdate: 10 May 1990 Next → “I play my part on my stage. I tell what I can to form the perfect answer. But that answer cannot come before all are ready to hear. So I tell what I can to form the perfect answer. Sometimes my anger at the fire is evident. Sometimes it is not anger, really. It may appear as such, but could it be a clue? The fire I speak of is not a kind fire.” Audrey Horne takes a job at her father's department store to help Cooper with his investigations Hank Jennings returns from prison to the Double-R Diner. James Hurley and Donna Hayward enlist Maddy in their search for Laura's killer. She finds a cassette tape hidden in her bedroom. The blood on Leo Johnson's shirt (found at Jacques Renault's flat) is not that of Laura Palmer. Cooper and Truman have tea with the Log Lady and discover a macabre crime scene in the woods. It seems that the Log Lady's Log is capable of observing events. The Log Lady had been expecting Cooper and Truman to call; she even said that they were late. Does this imply some sort of psychic ability on her part? Laura and Ronette were both present at Jacques Renault's cabin in the woods. Waldo, Jacques' mynah bird, witnessed the events at the cabin and Cooper finds a One-Eyed Jack's token with the "J" missing. Audrey spies on her father's secret assignation wtih Catherine Martell in his office. Leo Johnson is attacked by Hank Jennings at his cabin. He is then shot by Shelly when he tries to hit her. Benjamin Horne meets Josie in his office. She has found the second (false) set of accounts. Cooper returns to his hotel room to find Audrey waiting for him in bed. Unanswered Questions Why does the Log Lady alone hear the "voice" of her log? Is there in fact anything there, or is she just hallucinating / dreaming that she hears a voice? Perhaps the Log is a link with another world. Truman says that there is something mysterious in the local woods; perhaps the Log is a link to these powers. Another possibility is that the Log is inhabited by the spirit of Margaret's husband. Maybe he communicates with her through the Log. Perhaps he is in the White Lodge, How did Laura and Ronette get from the cabin to the train car? Did Jacques take them? (See Lonely Souls ). What useful information will be gained from Waldo the bird? What is Hank's connection to Josie? Whatever link there is between them, she seems very scared of him. Perhaps he is in possession of information that could damage her, or perhaps he has some other hold over her, perhaps related to the killing of the vagrant that caused him to be jailed. (See The Last Evening ). Now that James and Donna have Maddy's help, what are they going to do? (See Realization Time ). Does Ben Horne know what Battis is doing? If not, how will he react when he finds out? CAST LIST EPISODES CHARACTERS

title: 6 - Realization Time | Twin Peaks
text: 6 - Realization Time | Twin Peaks ← Previous 6 - Realization Time Written by Harley Peyton Directed by Caleb Deschanel Original Airdate: 17 May 1990 Next → “Beauty is in the eye of the beholder. Yet there are those who open many eyes. Eyes are the mirror of the soul, someone has said. So we look closely at the eyes to see the nature of the soul. Sometimes when we see the eyes-those horrible times when we see the eyes, eyes that ... that have no soul-then we know a darkness, then we wonder: where is the beauty? There is none if the eyes are soulless.” Agent Cooper lets the seductive Audrey down easy by having a night-long talk with her about life and love. Lucy continues to treat Deputy Andy coldly. She receives a phone call from a Dr. Stanicek. Audrey Horne, having taken a job at her father's department store, discovers that Emory Battis, the manager, is sending girls from the perfume counter to work at One-Eyed Jack's. Unknown to Cooper, Audrey goes undercover as a hostess there and persuades Blackie to hire her. Cooper and Bookhouse Boy Big Ed decide to pay a special visit to One-Eyed Jack's to find Jacques Renault who, having fled the country, now lives on the Canadian side of the border. Josie Packard shares her suspicions with Truman about Catherine and Ben's plan to burn the sawmill. That is why she took photos of them at the motel. However Catherine learns that both Ben Horne and Josie are planning to murder her. A wounded Leo, now a fugitive, learns about Jacques' mynah bird at the police station and plots to kill it. Waldo is shot by Leo but not before its voice is recorded on Cooper's dictaphone implicating Leo. The Icelandic businessmen still have not signed the Ghostwood Estates business deal so Ben Horne gets Jerry to take them to One-Eyed Jack's to persuade them. Ben makes a call to Leo to execute the burning down of the sawmill. He then makes another call to Hank Jennings to murder Leo, as well as Catherine, when the arson job at the sawmill is complete. Dr. Jacoby receives a phone call from Maddy pretending to be the dead Laura Palmer which lures him away from his office so James and Donna can search it to find the missing cassette tape. Bobby plants a stash of cocaine on James' motorbike while he is inside. Unanswered Questions Why is Lucy treating Deputy Andy so badly? Bobby Briggs watched "Laura" (Maddy) at the Gazebo, but someone else was watching both of them. Who? CAST LIST EPISODES CHARACTERS

title: 7 - The Last Evening | Twin Peaks
text: 7 - The Last Evening | Twin Peaks ← Previous 7 - The Last Evening Written by Mark Frost Directed by Mark Frost Original Airdate: 24 May 1990 Next → “A drunken man walks in a way that is quite impossible for a sober man to imitate, and vice versa. An evil man has a way, no matter how clever-to the trained eye, his way will show itself. Am I being too secretive? No. One can never answer questions at the wrong moment. Life, like music, has a rhythm. This particular song will end with three sharp sounds, like deathly drumbeats.” Dr. Jacoby heads for his rendezvous with "Laura Palmer" and suffers a heart attack when he is attacked by an unknown assailant. Nadine takes an overdose of pills. At One-Eyed Jack's, Cooper's 'sting' works on Jacques Renault. He discovers that Laura and Ronette met Jacques and Leo at Jacques' cabin. Laura had sex with both Leo and Jacques. Waldo attacked her in a fit of jealously. The plastic fragment was from a One-Eyed Jack's gambling chip that Leo told her to bite. Leo hit Jacques who passed out and, when he awoke, Leo and the girls had gone - presumably to the abandoned train car. Deputy Andy shoots Jacques Renault as he tries to escape capture. Lucy is impressed and tells Andy she is pregnant. Hank Jennings' evil influence spreads, engulfing Josie Packard. It appears Hank murdered Andrew Packard on Josie's orders. He went to prison to cover his tracks, and was paid $90,000 by Josie. However, he still wants more, and is prepared to blackmail her to get it. Leland Palmer, his mental state deteriorating rapidly, kills Jacques Renault in the hospital. Leo takes his revenge and leaves Shelly to die in the sawmill, which he set alight. Both Shelly and Catherine were in the sawmill, attempting to escape. Pete Martell enters the burning building looking for Catherine. Hank shoots Leo Johnson (on Ben Horne's orders) after Leo set the sawmill alight. But Bobby Briggs sees Hank shoot Leo. Cooper believes that Leo was Laura's killer. Back at the hotel, Cooper is shot by an unknown assailant. Unanswered Questions Who shot agent Cooper? Who attacked Dr. Jacoby? Is it the same person? Who was the "mystery man" that Laura spoke of? How did Leland know that it was Jacques that had been arrested for Laura's murder, and not Dr. Jacoby? Will Catherine, Shelly and Pete escape the fire? Is Leo dead? Will Bobby tell the Police that it was Hank? CAST LIST EPISODES CHARACTERS

title: 8 - May The Giant Be With You | Twin Peaks
text: 8 - May The Giant Be With You | Twin Peaks ← Previous 8 - May The Giant Be With You Written by Mark Frost Directed by David Lynch Original Airdate: 30 September 1990 Next → “Hello again. Can you see through a wall? Can you see through human skin? X-rays see through solid, or so-called solid objects. There are things in life that exist, and yet our eyes cannot see them. Have you ever seen something startling that others cannot see? Why are some things kept from our vision? Is life a puzzle? I am filled with questions. Sometimes my questions are answered. In my heart, I can tell if the answer is correct. I am my own judge. In a dream, are all the characters really you? Different aspects of you? Do answers come in dreams? One more thing: I grew up in the woods. I understand many things because of the woods. Trees standing together, growing alongside one another, providing so much. I chew pitch gum. On the outside, let's say of the ponderosa pine, sometimes pitch oozes out. Runny pitch is no good to chew. Hard, brittle pitch is no good. But in between there exists a firm, slightly crusted pitch with such a flavor. This is the pitch I chew.” A shot and bleeding Agent Cooper has visions of a Giant who tells him three clues to help with the investigation: There is a man in a smiling bag. The owls are not what they seem. Without chemicals, he points. At One-Eyed Jack's, Audrey escapes being recognised by her father but finds that she's a prisoner there. Both Catherine and Josie are missing after the sawmill fire, while Shelly and Pete are in the hospital after escaping the blaze. After killing Jacques, Leland's hair has turned white. His mood has changed drastically: he sings and dances merrily. Albert Rosenfield returns to Twin Peaks, much to the dismay of Truman's team. Maddy has visions of BOB in her carpet. James remains in jail after being framed by Bobby who planted Leo's cocaine stash in his motorcycle. Big Ed maintains a bedside vigil for the comatose Nadine after a suicide attempt. Leo remains in a coma after being shot by the murderous Hank. Donna, following a tip from the Log Lady, decides to investigate the Double-R's Meals on Wheels program where Laura worked. When Cooper retires for the night, the Giant returns in a vision to tell him: Don't search for all the answers at once. A path is formed by laying one stone at a time. One person saw the third man; three have seen him, yes, but not his body. One only known to you, ready now to talk. A stirring Ronette relives Laura's murder: she remembers BOB being at the cabin and also remembers BOB killing Laura. Unanswered Questions Who is the Giant? Why is he helping Cooper, and why can he only give clues, not give Cooper the answers? Who has forbidden him to say more? What has happened to Catherine? Is she dead? Is she in hiding? It is clear that BOB killed Laura. Who is BOB? Why has no one seen him in Twin Peaks, when he was definitely present at the train car? According to Cooper's interpretation of his dream, MIKE killed BOB. Therefore, is BOB a ghost? Or is BOB inhabiting someone else's body, in much the same way that the Log Lady's husband may inhabit her log? (See Demons ). Leland Palmer's attitude has changed. From the peak of despair, he has miraculously changed into someone with every appearance of not having a care in the world. Is this because he thinks that Laura's murderer has been "brought to justice"? Or is something more sinister afoot? (See Demons ). CAST LIST EPISODES CHARACTERS

title: 9 - Coma | Twin Peaks
text: 9 - Coma | Twin Peaks ← Previous 9 - Coma Written by Harley Peyton Directed by David Lynch Original Airdate: 6 October 1990 Next → "As above, so below. The human being finds himself, or herself, in the middle. There is as much space outside the human, proportionately, as inside. "Stars, moons, and planets remind us of protons, neutrons, and electrons. Is there a bigger being walking with all the stars within? Does our thinking affect what goes on outside us, and what goes on inside us? I think it does. "Where does creamed corn figure into the workings of the universe? What really is creamed corn? Is it a symbol for something else?" Still investigating Cooper's shooting, Albert Rosenfield tells Cooper that his former partner and mentor, Windom Earle, has escaped from an insane asylum and may come after him. Meanwhile, Donna meets the mysterious Mrs. Tremond and her weird grandson on Laura's meals-on-wheels route who direct Donna to the home of Harold Smith who was a special friend of Laura's. Ronette Pulaski awakens from her coma, is not responsive, but reacts frantically when she is shown a drawing of BOB. With Catherine missing and presumed dead, Ben and Jerry Horne debate destroying the sawmill ledgers, while Leland, still acting erratically, apparently ruins the business deal with the Icelandic investors by letting slip about the sawmill fire. Leland however spots a Wanted Poster of the image of BOB in Ben Horne's office and gasps " I know him ... when I was a little boy ... he lived right next door ". Andy angrily tells Lucy that he's sterile and wants an explanation why she's pregnant. At One-Eyed Jack's, Audrey is uncovered by a vengeful Blackie as she interrogates Emory Battis and learns how Laura came to work there and that her father is the owner of the place. Laura worked at One-Eyed Jack's, but she was still using drugs and was thrown out. Bobby persuades Shelly not to press domestic abuse charges on the brain-damaged Leo so they can take care of him and live off the insurance money. At the prompting of the Log Lady, Major Briggs delivers a message to Cooper about top-secret work he has done for the U.S. Government in researching UFOs. He received outer space messages which read " The owls are not what they seem " and " Cooper, Cooper ". Donna becomes jealous when James develops an attraction to Maddy, who has a frightening vision of Killer BOB, as does Cooper when an owl's face is superimposed over BOB's. Unanswered Questions " The owls are not what they seem ". What does this signify? BOB's face was seen with an owl superimposed on top, and owls have always been present, observing key events. Does this imply that BOB was / is an owl? What would this mean: an "owl" as they appear to us, or a person with an owl's predatory characteristics? The Log is in communication with whoever sent the message to Cooper. The messages from the Log seem to imply a complete understanding of what is going on. The Log Lady, in her description of the night Laura died, used the expression the owls were flying. Does this mean that the "owls" i.e. BOB were active that night? If BOB is a "spirit", inhabiting different bodies, does that mean that BOB was changing hosts? Or even taking control of his host? CAST LIST EPISODES CHARACTERS

title: 10 - The Man Behind Glass | Twin Peaks
text: 10 - The Man Behind Glass | Twin Peaks ← Previous 10 - The Man Behind Glass Written by Robert Engels Directed by Lesli Linka Glatter Original Airdate: 13 October 1990 Next → "Letters are symbols. They are building blocks of words which form our languages. Languages help us communicate. Even with complicated languages used by intelligent people, misunderstanding is a common occurrence. "We write things down sometimes: letters, words, hoping they will serve us and those with whom we wish to communicate. Letters and words, calling out for understanding." Cooper and Agent Rosenfield are alerted when an attempt is made on Ronette Pulaski's life at the hospital. The letter "B" is found inserted under her finger nail. They now have an "R" (from Laura Palmer), a "B" and a "T" (from Teresa Banks whose body was found one year earlier). Meanwhile, Donna meets with the reclusive Harold Smith, an orchid cultivator, whom she asks about Laura. He explains that Laura wanted him to contact Donna if anything ever happened to Laura as she would " ask a lot of questions ". Leland comes to the police station after seeing the police sketch of Killer BOB claiming to have known the mysterious man from his childhood. He remembers his name as Robertson and that he used to flick matches at him saying " You want to play with fire, little boy? ". Elsewhere, Lucy meets with the suave and vain Dick Tremayne (Designer Menswear - Horne's Department Store) and confides that she's pregnant from a brief fling they had and the baby may be his. At One-Eyed Jack's, Audrey is held prisoner by Blackie and Emory whom are under the employment of Jean Renault who plans to extract a ransom from Benjamin Horne, as well as kill Cooper whom he blames for the deaths of his brothers Bernard and Jacques. Phillip Michael Gerard, the one-armed man, while selling shoes to Agent Truman has a seizure after seeing the sketch of Killer BOB and emerges from the bathroom as his alter ego MIKE. He disappears but Cooper finds a syringe on the floor of the bathroom which reminds him of the Giant's third clue - " Without chemicals, he points ". The mysterious Asian man staying at the Great Northern Hotel continues to follow Cooper around. At the hospital, Nadine Hurley awakens from her coma but, to Big Ed's bewilderment, she thinks she's 18 years old and in high school. Nearby, Dr. Jacoby is hypnotised by Cooper to look back into that night when Jacques Renault was murdered and remembers seeing Leland carry out the murder and smelling engine oil. Maddy is upset because people " keep confusing her with Laura ". Sheriff Truman and Cooper come to Leland's house to arrest him for the murder of Jacques Renault. Also, Donna continues to become jealous over James hanging around Maddy and runs to Harold Smith for comfort. She finds a diary of Laura's at his house. Unanswered Questions Who is the mysterious Asian man following Cooper? CAST LIST EPISODES CHARACTERS

title: 11 - Laura's Secret Diary | Twin Peaks
text: 11 - Laura's Secret Diary | Twin Peaks ← Previous 11 - Laura's Secret Diary Written by Jerry Stahl, Mark Frost, Harley Peyton & Robert Engels Directed by Todd Holland Original Airdate: 20 October 1990 Next → "Miscommunication sometimes leads to arguments, and arguments sometimes lead to fights. Anger is usually present in arguments and fights. Anger is an emotion, usually classified as a negative emotion. Negative emotions can cause severe problems in our environment and to the health of our body. "Happiness, usually classified as a positive emotion, can bring good health to our body, and spread positive vibrations into our environment. Sometimes when we are ill, we are not on our best behavior. By ill, I mean any of the following: physically ill, emotionally ill, mentally ill, and/or spiritually ill." Cooper and Sheriff Truman arrest Leland after he confesses that he was the one who murdered Jacques Renault in his hospital bed as well as the one who attacked Dr. Jacoby that night under the delusion that he was protecting Laura. Andy asks Dr. Hayward about taking a sperm test to see if he really is sterile. Hank Jennings encourages Norma to spruce up the Double-R Diner when news circulates that a shadowy travel writer and food critic named M.T. Wentz, whom no one has ever met, may be coming to Twin Peaks. Meanwhile, Jean Renault delivers a videotape of the captive Audrey to Ben Horne and demands a huge ransom for her return and he wants Cooper to be the drop-off man. Ben Horne is prepared to help Renault kill Cooper if it will get his daughter back. On returning to One-Eyed Jack's, Renault murders Emory Battis for treating the captive Audrey badly. Cooper asks Truman to help him with investigating Audrey's kidnapping. Donna continues to meet with Harold Smith who shows her Laura Palmer's secret diary which Laura gave to him for safekeeping, which increases Donna's interest. Josie returns to Twin Peaks claiming to have been in Seattle on business where she learns from Pete that Catherine died in the sawmill fire. Josie also refuses to give Truman an explanation about where she was during this time. A mysterious Japanese businessman, Tojamura, checks into the Great Northern Hotel. The mysterious Asian man, identifying himself as Jonathan Lee, Josie's "cousin" from Hong Kong, meets with Josie and informs her that her job in Twin Peaks of collecting the insurance from the sawmill fire is nearly done and that their boss wants them back in Hong Kong soon. Josie is working to some sort of deadline, one which Jonathan is there to enforce. It appears that she is working for a "Mr. Eckhardt". Jonathan also beats up Hank Jennings for threatening Josie. Unanswered Questions Who is Jonathan? Why is he in Twin Peaks? What is Josie's "mission", and why is she working for "Mr. Eckhardt"? Who is he? Who is Tojamura? Is he the mystery M.T. Wentz? Will Cooper suspect Ben Horne's request is a trap? CAST LIST EPISODES CHARACTERS

title: 12 - The Orchid's Curse | Twin Peaks
text: 12 - The Orchid's Curse | Twin Peaks ← Previous 12 - The Orchid's Curse Written by Barry Pullman Directed by Graeme Clifford Original Airdate: 27 October 1990 Next → "Sometimes nature plays tricks on us and we imagine we are something other than what we truly are. Is this a key to life in general? Or the case of the two-headed schizophrenic? Both heads thought the other was following itself. Finally, when one head wasn't looking, the other shot the other right between the eyes, and, of course, killed himself." Cooper finally finds Audrey's message which she slipped under his door and figures out that she is being held captive at One-Eyed Jack's and asks Truman to help him sneak into the place to rescue her. Bobby and Shelly plan making over her house to assist Leo's return to take bed-care of him, while Mr. Pinkle gets stuck in a mechanical device showing them how to work it. Leland Palmer's court hearing is held at the Roadhouse where Judge Sternwood releases him on his own will. Judge Sternwood also rules that Leo Johnson is not competent to stand trial for the sawmill fire. Hank is ordered by Ben Horne to follow Cooper to make sure he delivers the ransom money and get Audrey back. Big Ed brings the crazy and delusional Nadine home from the hospital. The mysterious Japanese businessman, Tojamura, approaches Ben Horne and offers him a $5 million cheque for the purchase of Ghostwood Estates. Andy, covering for Lucy desk job while she's visiting her sister in Tacoma, learns that he is not sterile after all. Blackie is murdered, like Battis, by Jean Renault when her usefulness runs out. At One-Eyed Jack's, Jean Renault plots with Blackie's sister, Nancy, to steal the ransom money for themselves after it is delivered. Cooper and Truman escape with Audrey from One-Eyed Jack's after Hawk deals with an unwelcome bodyguard. They are seen by Hank who, in turn, is seen by Jean Renault. Donna enlists Maddy's help to help her steal Laura's secret diary away from Harold Smith who has become dangerously unstable and catches them in the act. Unanswered Questions Will Harold Smith kill Donna and Maddy? It seems that Donna's betrayal of him as plunged him into madness. What is he capable of? Who is Tojamura? (See Lonely Souls ). How did Hawk know that Cooper and Truman would be going to One-Eyed Jack's? His excuse was pretty feeble. Does he regularly listen to Truman's conversations? CAST LIST EPISODES CHARACTERS

title: 13 - Demons | Twin Peaks
text: 13 - Demons | Twin Peaks ← Previous 13 - Demons Written by Harley Peyton and Robert Engels Directed by Lesli Linka Glatter Original Airdate: 3 November 1990 Next → "Sometimes we want to hide from ourselves - we do not want to be us - it is too difficult to be us. It is at these times that we turn to drugs or alcohol or behavior to help us forget that we are ourselves. "This of course is only a temporary solution to a problem which is going to keep returning, and sometimes these temporary solutions are worse for us than the original problem. "Yes, it is a dilemma. Is there an answer? Of course there is: as a wise person said with a smile: 'The answer is within the question.'" Donna and Maddy find themselves at the mercy of an enraged Harold Smith who has gone mad. Donna and Maddy are rescued by James but are forced to leave Laura's secret diary behind. Cooper informs Ben of his rescue of Audrey from One-Eyed Jack's, and Truman identifies Jean Renault as the mastermind behind the whole thing. Meanwhile, Shelly Johnson and Bobby Briggs hold a "welcome home" party for the catatonic Leo, but are disappointed of the low amount of insurance money they get. They take out their vengeance on the comatose Leo by humiliating him. Jonathan threatens Josie that he will kill Sheriff Truman if she refuses to return to Hong Kong with him. Josie then demands the insurance money for the sawmill from Ben who gives her Tojamura's $5 million check. Josie then leaves with Jonathan, despite desperate pleas from Harry. Later Gordon Cole, Cooper's superior, arrives in Twin Peaks to assist Cooper's investigation, warn Cooper of threats and to help find the mysterious one-armed man who holds a clue to the identity of Laura Palmer's killer. He also warns Cooper of Windom Earle, from whom he delivers a cryptic note regarding a chess move. Big Ed continues to deal with the crazy Nadine and her super-human powers. Maddy says goodbye to James as she prepares to leave Twin Peaks. Interrogating the One-Armed Man, Cooper withholds his medication whereupon MIKE emerges who gives them information about the evil spirit Killer BOB, who inhabits a person that lives in Twin Peaks. MIKE, like BOB, is an "inhabiting spirit", who has been using Gerard's body to track down BOB - who was once his "familiar" - to stop him from killing again. BOB is a spirit who takes over peoples' bodies and uses them to feed. BOB's food is fear and the "pleasures". BOB is now at the Great Northern Hotel. Unanswered Questions As Harold Smith had Laura's secret diary, could he have killed her? Who is BOB's current host? Why did Windom Earle send Cooper a chess move? What will Harold Smith do now that he is "unclean"? Josie obviously did not want to leave. Why did she have to go? CAST LIST EPISODES CHARACTERS

title: 14 - Lonely Souls | Twin Peaks
text: 14 - Lonely Souls | Twin Peaks ← Previous 14 - Lonely Souls Written by Mark Frost Directed by David Lynch Original Airdate: 10 November 1990 Next → "A poem as lovely as a tree: As the night wind blows, the boughs move to and fro. The rustling, the magic rustling that brings on the dark dream. The dream of suffering and pain. Pain for the victim, pain for the inflictor of pain. A circle of pain, a circle of suffering. Woe to the ones who behold the pale horse." Cooper, Truman, and Cole take the One-Armed Man to the Great Northern Hotel, which is hosting a USO stop-over, in their search for BOB where MIKE shrieks and panics when Ben Horne approaches. Audrey tells her father that she knows about Laura's employment at One-Eyed Jack's, and she tells Cooper about Ben's involvement whereupon Cooper and Truman arrest him as a suspect in Laura's murder. Hawk searches Harold Smith's house for Laura Palmer's secret diary only to find Harold dead from a suicide, and his house and Laura's diary torn apart by him. His last note was J'ai une âme solitaire , which is French for I have a lonely soul . These are the same words that Mrs. Tremond's grandson (the Creamed Corn Kid) said to Donna. Finances strain the relationship between Shelly and Bobby having misjudged the money due them. Leland Palmer tries to discourage Maddy from going home. Meanwhile, Shelly tells Norma that she's quitting working at the Double-R Diner to care for Leo. Bobby and Mike find a mini-cassette in Leo's boots. Tojamura plans to buy the Ghostwood Estates and, when he learns of Ben's arrest, goes to the Blue Pines B&B and surprises Pete Martell by revealing that 'he' is actually the missing Catherine Martell in disguise. The Log Lady knows that something was going to happen at the Roadhouse, where Cooper saw the Giant. In the climatic twist at the Roadhouse, Cooper receives another message from the Giant who knows that BOB is killing Maddy across town and tells Cooper that "It is happening again". Maddy is alerted by the vile smell of burning oil and tragically learns the identity of Laura's killer and who BOB inhabits. Leland Palmer, possessed by BOB, drugs Sarah and then murders Maddy and inserts a capital "O" under her fingernail. Leland is, and always has been, the killer. Unanswered Questions How much of Leland's actions have been Leland and what has been BOB? Does Leland know what BOB is doing? Does Leland have a hope of ridding himself of BOB? What is on the cassette which Bobby found in Leo's boots? Where has Catherine been? How did she survive? Who is the Giant? Why does he keep leaving cryptic clues for Cooper? BOB seemed under the impression that Maddy was Laura during the murder. Does this mean that he killed her simply to relive the experience of the first murder? If the burning oil smell accompanies BOB's appearance, does that mean that Leland was under the influence of BOB when he attacked Jacoby, as Jacoby sensed the same smell at the Gazebo? CAST LIST EPISODES CHARACTERS

title: 15 - Drive With A Dead Girl | Twin Peaks
text: 15 - Drive With A Dead Girl | Twin Peaks ← Previous 15 - Drive With A Dead Girl Written by Scott Frost Directed by Caleb Deschanel Original Airdate: 17 November 1990 Next → "Food is interesting. For instance, why do we need to eat? Why are we never satisfied with just the right amount of food to maintain good health and proper energy? We always seem to want more and more. "When eating too much, the proper balance is disturbed and ill health follows. Of course, eating too little food throws the balance off in the opposite direction and there is the ill health coming at us again. "Balance is the key. Balance is the key to many things. Do we understand balance? The word 'balance' has seven letters. Seven is difficult to balance, but not impossible if we are able to divide. There are, of course, the pros and cons of division." James Hurley and Donna Hayward miss the chance to say goodbye to Maddy. Leland Palmer (under the direction of BOB) hides the dead Maddy Ferguson in his golf bag and goes for a joyride. Leland has now been totally possessed by BOB, and dances convulsively, as well as taking pleasure in the pain of others. All aspects of Leland's character have been over-ridden. Lucy arrives back in Twin Peaks with her visiting, equally simpleton older sister, Gwen Morton, while Andy tells Lucy he wants to get back together with her. With Ben Horne in jail for Laura Palmer's murder, Jerry tries to arrange a defense for him. Cooper doubts Ben's guilt, but Truman thinks otherwise. Bobby decides to blackmail Ben as the recording (which he found in Leo's boots) reveals Ben giving Leo instructions to burn down the sawmill. Since Ben is already in jail, this might be hard. Norma Jennings' estranged mother, Vivian Smythe, brings her new husband Ernie Niles for a visit, while Hank reappears after being gone for several days and reveals to have known Ernie from time in prison. Ernie is posing as a businessman and has probably told many more lies about his past as well. The One-Armed Man escapes from police custody with a warning that BOB is nearby. Cooper's and Truman's search for BOB gets a boost from the One-Armed Man, who is suffering from an identity crisis. Pete Martell later visits Ben in jail with a taunting audio message from Catherine saying that she only will back up his alibi if he surrenders all his property over to her. It may be assumed that everything Leland has done since Maddy's murder is BOB alone. It could also be argued that everything Leland has done since his hair turned white (like BOB's) has been BOB. However, there are several occasions on which Leland is kind, thoughtful and considerate, such as when he comforted Maddy before his arrest. It is hard to imagine BOB behaving like this, even if it was a disguise. It can be assumed that BOB intended to kill Cooper with the golf club. MIKE's re-capture was all that saved him. Maddy Ferguson's body has been found. Unanswered Questions How much of Leland's past actions has been "BOB"? How much longer can "BOB" / Leland go undiscovered? What will Bobby do with the cassette? How will Ben respond to blackmail? Will Ben sign the sawmill over to Catherine? What about the Ghostwood project? CAST LIST EPISODES CHARACTERS

title: 16 - Arbitrary Law | Twin Peaks
text: 16 - Arbitrary Law | Twin Peaks ← Previous 16 - Arbitrary Law Written by Mark Frost, Harley Peyton and Robert Engels Directed by Tim Hunter Original Airdate: 1 December 1990 Next → "So now the sadness comes: the revelation. There is a depression after an answer is given. It was almost fun not knowing. Yes, now we know. At least we know what we sought in the beginning. "But there is still the question: why? And this question will go on and on until the final answer comes. Then the knowing is so full, there is no room for questions." With the discovery of Maddy Ferguson's dead body, Cooper and Truman, aided by Albert Rosenfeld, push their investigation into full-drive. Cooper asks Truman to give him 24 hours to prove who murdered Laura Palmer. Norma continues to deal with her difficult mother who constantly criticises and puts down her attempts to bond. Donna Hayward is surprised by Deputy Andy's knowledge of French. Mrs. Tremond and her grandson have vanished without a trace. It appears that they were never actually there. Donna discovers the appearance of a different Mrs. Tremond (not the old lady and her grandson - who were apparently spirits). Donna follows a lead from the late Harold Smith leading to a mysterious page from Laura's secret diary, from which Cooper discovers both he and Laura shared the same dream. Ben Horne's business fortunes hit an all-time low as Catherine, disguised once again as Tojamura, tricks him into signing away the sawmill and regains control. She then abandons her disguise as "Tojamura". Leland / BOB learns about Laura's secret diary from Donna, who learns about Maddy's murder from Sheriff Truman. James does not take the news of Maddy's fate easily and hits the road on his motorcycle. Andy learns about Lucy's tryst with the smug Dick Tremayne, and Lucy tells them that she's keeping her baby and will choose one of them to be the father. Cooper assembles all the suspects present at the Roadhouse. While there, the Waiter offers people sticks of gum and tells Leland "that gum you like is going to come back in style", prompting Cooper to remember his earlier dream of the Red Room and a flashback vision of Laura Palmer who reveals the identity of the killer and of Killer BOB. The Giant returns Cooper's ring. Cooper realises that Leland is the host to BOB but arrests Ben Horne. While Ben is about to be imprisoned again, Cooper and Sheriff Truman throw Leland into the interrogation room, where he goes into a manic fit and, as BOB, confesses that he murdered Laura Palmer and Maddy Ferguson. When Cooper, Albert, Sheriff Truman and Hawk leave, BOB chants a poem ending with the phrase "Fire walk with me." The water sprinklers turn on and BOB forces Leland to commit suicide by ramming his head into a steel door. BOB vacates Leland's body and Leland, in his dying moments, reveals the nature of his possession. Cooper comforts Leland through his last moments and Leland dies after seeing a vision of Laura. Cooper, Albert, Sheriff Truman and Major Briggs walk through the woods outside of Twin Peaks discussing Leland's possession and death. Albert concludes that BOB is just "the evil that men do" and Sheriff Truman questions where BOB might have gone to. An unseen character then runs through the woods and an owl flies out from a large white light. Unanswered Questions Did BOB kill Leland as we see him standing beneath the water sprinkler, or did Leland kill himself when he remembered what he had done to Laura, Maddy, Theresa and Sarah, and all the other people whose lives had been disturbed by BOB's actions? Was it BOB or Tremayne's cigar that set off the sprinklers? This is a typical piece of Twin Peaks ambiguity. BOB, the spirit of "fire", whose departure from Leland, his host of many years, coincided with the starting of the sprinkler system seems perfectly capable of causing metaphorical fire. However, Tremayne's smoke could equally have done the job. Perhaps it was the water that finally quenched the fire of BOB in Leland. CAST LIST EPISODES CHARACTERS

title: 17 - Dispute Between Brothers | Twin Peaks
text: 17 - Dispute Between Brothers | Twin Peaks ← Previous 17 - Dispute Between Brothers Written by Tricia Brock Directed by Tina Rathborne Original Airdate: 8 December 1990 Next → "Complications set in - yes, complications. How many times have we heard: 'it's simple'? Nothing is simple. We live in a world where nothing is simple. Each day, just when we think we have a handle on things, suddenly some new element is introduced and everything is complicated once again. What is the secret? What is the secret to simplicity, to the pure and simple life? Are our appetites, our desires undermining us? Is the cart in front of the horse?" Three days after Leland's death, following his confession to having killed Laura Palmer while under the control of the evil spirit BOB, Sarah tries to adjust herself to this turn of events with Cooper's explanation. A wake is held for Leland Palmer where Dougie Milford, publisher of the Twin Peaks Gazette, antagonises his brother, Mayor Dwayne Milford. Big Ed and Dr. Jacoby persuade the Vice-Principal of Twin Peaks High School to enroll Nadine as a student to satisfy her delusion that she's still in high school. Audrey says goodbye to Cooper who tells her how his first love died while he should have been protecting her, and how his then partner Windom Earle went mad. Bobby unsuccessfully tries to blackmail the distraught Ben Horne with the incriminating tape of him talking with Leo, while Audrey gives Bobby some advice about how to confront her father. Catherine pays a visit to the sheriff's station and tells Truman that a "guardian angel" saved her life at the sawmill fire. Dick Tremayne has given up smoking and embraces fatherhood. As Cooper prepares to leave Twin Peaks with the Laura Palmer case closed, a new twist comes when Roger Hardy, an agent with FBI Internal Affairs, and a Canadian Mountie named Preston King, show up and suspend Cooper for his unauthorised actions in Canada. Mountie King also reveals that Cooper's rescue of Audrey Horne from One-Eyed Jack's ruined a sting operation set up to arrest Jean Renault. The drugs used for the sting will be subsequently found in Cooper's car. Norma's mother, Vivian, leaves town after revealing that she's the M.T. Wentz that everyone talks about and the one responsible for the bad review of the Double-R Diner. Hank takes Ernie Niles off on an impromptu "hunting trip" to One-Eyed Jack's where they meet with Jean Renault who wants them to traffic some cocaine for him. Josie Packard reappears and collapses at Truman's house. On Cooper's fishing trip, Major Briggs reveals the existence of the White Lodge before he is mysteriously abducted. Unanswered Questions Where has Josie Packard been? Why has she come back? Who or what has abducted Major Briggs? CAST LIST EPISODES CHARACTERS

title: 18 - Masked Ball | Twin Peaks
text: 18 - Masked Ball | Twin Peaks ← Previous 18 - Masked Ball Written by Barry Pullman Directed by Duwayne Dunham Original Airdate: 15 December 1990 Next → "Is life like a game of chess? Are our present moves important for future success? I think so. We paint our future with every present brush stroke. "Painting. Colours. Shapes. Textures. Composition. Repetition of shapes. Contrast. Let nature guide us. Nature is the great teacher. Who is the principal? "Sometimes jokes are welcome. Like the one about the kid who said: 'I enjoyed school. It was just the principle of the thing.'" Mrs. Briggs worries about her husband's disappearance after which Cooper and Truman investigate his research with the Air Force which involved in classified dealings with paranormal events which includes an unofficial search for places called the White Lodge and the Black Lodge. Gordon Cole phones to offer Cooper his full support and advises "Let a smile be your umbrella". Truman defends Cooper's activities at One-Eyed Jack's, which are under investigation by the FBI and DEA but Cooper refuses to offer a defense to Agent Hardy and instead confuses the IA agent with more mystical talk. James Hurley stops in a small town several miles from Twin Peaks where a young wealthy heiress, named Evelyn Marsh, picks him up and offers him a job to fix her husband's car. Dick Tremayne tries to train himself for parenthood when he takes a young, rambunctious orphan boy, named Little Nicky, under his wing to impress Lucy. Later, a transvestite DEA agent, named Dennis (Denise) Bryson, arrives to investigate the drug charges against Cooper. Back in Twin Peaks, Nadine tries to win Mike Nelson's affections with her super-human strength which instead nets the eyes of the school's wrestling coach. Josie who has shown up on Truman's doorstep reveals to him that she has run away from her employer, a South African gangster named Thomas Eckhardt, who is now looking for her. All of Twin Peaks gathers for the wedding of Doug Milford to a young gold digger, named Lana Budding. Windom Earle makes a move by sending Cooper a note and a cassette tape. Hank interrupts Ben Horne's reminiscences about the past with grim reality. Ben Horne is further distraught after learning from Hank that Jean Renault has ousted him as the owner of One-Eyed Jack's and Hank is now under Renault's employment. Andy kicks up his heels with DEA Agent Bryson at the wedding reception of Dougie Milford and his young bride. When Truman refuses to help Josie, she goes to Catherine who agrees to help under her own conditions. It is also revealed that Andrew Packard, whom Eckhardt hired Josie to kill and who later sub-contracted Hank to do the deed, is alive and plans with Catherine to bring down Josie. Unanswered Questions Where is Major Briggs? Where has Andrew Packard been all this time? CAST LIST EPISODES CHARACTERS

title: 19 - The Black Widow | Twin Peaks
text: 19 - The Black Widow | Twin Peaks ← Previous Next → 19 - The Black Widow Written by Harley Peyton and Robert Engels Directed by Caleb Deschanel Original Airdate: 12 January 1991 “ Is a dog man's best friend? I had a dog. The dog was large. It ate my garden, all the plants, and much earth. The dog ate so much earth it died. Its body went back to the earth. I have a memory of this dog. The memory is all that I have left of my dog. He was black – and white. ” Ben Horne continues to slip deeper into insanity while Bobby tries to win his admiration by tailing Hank Jennings and photographs him in a drug dealing meeting. Cooper looks into real estate to buy in thought of staying in Twin Peaks and uncovers recent drug activity at a run-down house called Dead Dog Farm. Truman investigates when Dougie Milford dies from a heart attack on his wedding night, in which Mayor Milford insists that Lana Budding be charged with murder through sex. Nadine hears the call of organized sports and continues to try to win Mike Nelson's affections by body-slamming him while trying out for the school's wrestling team. At the Marsh estate, James learns more about Evelyn's troubled marriage from her chauffeur, (her brother Malcolm), but cannot resist temptation from the femme fatale. Elsewhere, Dick Tremayne takes Little Nicky out camping where the child's attitude scares him after learning from Nicky's case worker that his parents died under mysterious circumstances. Cooper and Truman receive a visit from a visiting Air Force colonel investigating Major Briggs' disappearance who tells them about the Major's top-secret search for the so-called White Lodge. Catherine and Pete Martell continue to gloat and taunt Josie who now works for them as a maid while they attempt a romantic candlelight dinner. Audrey helps Cooper prove his innocence of the drug dealing charges by showing him the photos Bobby took of Ernie Niles, Jean Renault, Hank Jennings and the corrupt Mountie King. Cooper gives the photos to Agent Bryson who arranges a sting at the Dead Dog Farm. Major Briggs reappears to his wife and Bobby in his house. Unanswered Questions Is Little Nicky the child of the Devil? Where has Major Briggs been while abducted? CAST LIST EPISODES CHARACTERS

title: 20 - Checkmate | Twin Peaks
text: 20 - Checkmate | Twin Peaks ← Previous Next → 20 - Checkmate Written by Harley Peyton Directed by Todd Holland Original Airdate: 19 January 1991 “ My husband died in a fire. No one can know my sorrow. My love is gone. Yet, I feel him near me. Sometimes I can almost see him. At night when the wind blows, I think of what he might have been. Again I wonder: why? “ When I see a fire, I feel my anger rising. This was not a friendly fire. This was not a forest fire. It was a fire *in the woods*. This is all I am permitted to say. ” Following Major Briggs' mysterious reappearance, Cooper and Truman are frustrated as they question him to learn his whereabouts during his absence. He appears to have three triangular scars below his right ear and all he remembers is a disturbing image of a giant owl. Cooper assists DEA Bryson and Truman with setting up Ernie Niles to arrest Jean Renault and Mountie King at Dead Dog Farm. But the sting goes bad due to Niles’ nervousness in which a stand-off ensues. Cooper then trades himself for Bryson and Niles and is held at gunpoint. Dick Tremayne persuades Deputy Andy to help investigate Little Nicky's past by visiting the Dorritt Home for Boys orphanage. Bobby has another argument with Shelly about taking care of the catatonic Leo, who does not remain that way for long James Hurley succumbs to Evelyn Marsh's plea for help and continues romancing Evelyn while being observed by her chauffeur / brother Malcolm. Mike Nelson continues being pursued by Nadine. Harry visits Josie (now working as Catherine's maid) and discovers how afraid she is. At the Great Northern Hotel, Audrey sees her father slipping further into insanity by re-enacting the Civil War in his office and thinking that he is General Robert E. Lee. A visit from an old lover interrupts him. Donna misses James and discovers his whereabouts from Big Ed. She will take his savings money to him. Meanwhile, Hank finally discovers the romantic relationship between Norma and Big Ed and, when he attempts to beat up Ed, he gets attacked and pulverized by the super-strong Nadine. Audrey asks Bobby for help with her father's condition. DEA Bryson brings food to the stand-off at Dead Dog Farm. Cooper grabs a gun she has concealed in her stockings and shoots Jean Renault. Cooper's nemesis Windom Earle makes a horrifying opening move. Unanswered Questions Why is Major Briggs' work 'classified'? What does Windom Earle intend? CAST LIST EPISODES CHARACTERS

title: 21 - Double Play | Twin Peaks
text: 21 - Double Play | Twin Peaks ← Previous Next → 21 - Double Play Written by Scott Frost Directed by Uli Edel Original Airdate: 2 February 1991 “ The heart – it is a physical organ, we all know. But how much more an emotional organ – this we also know. Love, like blood, flows from the heart. Are blood and love related? Does a heart pump blood as it pumps love? Is love the blood of the universe? ” Cooper discusses with Truman the opening moves by his former FBI partner, Windom Earle, over the discovery of a dead body which is the opening move of a deadly chess game where, when each pawn is taken, a person dies. Audrey Horne strikes a business deal with Bobby Briggs and asks Jerry Horne for help concerning Ben's delusion in re-enacting the Civil War, while Dr. Jacoby persuades Ben to push for a Confederate victory. Leo Johnson comes back to vicious life and attempts to kill Shelly; she stabs him in the leg and he flees into the woods. Andy confides to Lucy about his and Dick's suspicion concerning Little Nicky. Lucy then asks Dr. Hayward for help who then finally clears the mystery. At the Marsh estate, James Hurley meets Evelyn's husband for the first time, who seems to be a nice guy, and becomes more confused about his feelings for Evelyn. Back in Twin Peaks, Big Ed confides in 'Doc' Hayward about Nadine dating Mike Nelson. Cooper also confides to Truman the frightening, tragic history of his involvement with Earle's wife Caroline that may have pushed Earle over the edge. In the nearby town, Donna arrives with money for James, and instead meets Evelyn who tells her that James has left town already. Major Briggs staggers into the Sheriff's office and confides in Cooper and Truman about his work for the Air Force's classified search for the so-called White Lodge. He believes he was taken to the White Lodge during his abduction. Dr. Jacoby also clears Lana Budding of any misdeeds concerning the death of Dougie Milford, but it takes some persuasion to convince the elderly and senile Mayor Milford. Catherine Martell unveils an astonishing secret to a dumbfounded Pete – Andrew Packard is alive – and they let him in on their plans to bring down Josie by contacting her former boss / lover, the ruthless South African businessman Thomas Eckhardt, who arrives in Twin Peaks looking for Josie. Evelyn Marsh's husband is killed in a car crash. Malcolm is not her brother. James has been set up. He makes his escape and meets Donna who is still in town looking for him. After Leo escapes into the woods, pursued by owls, he arrives at a cabin housing the deranged Windom Earle Unanswered Questions How did Leo Johnson come back out of his coma? What will be Windom Earle's next move? CAST LIST EPISODES CHARACTERS

title: 22 - Slaves And Masters | Twin Peaks
text: 22 - Slaves And Masters | Twin Peaks ← Previous Next → 22 - Slaves And Masters Written by Harley Peyton and Robert Engels Directed by Diane Keaton Original Airdate: 9 February 1991 “ A death mask. Is there a reason for a death mask? It is barely a physical resemblance – in death, the muscles so relaxed, the face so without the animating spark. A death mask is almost an intrusion on a beautiful memory. And yet ... who could throw away the casting of a loved one? Who would not want to study it longingly, as the distant freight train blows its mournful tone? ” James Hurley becomes a fugitive when Evelyn's husband is found murdered. Donna Hayward makes a desperate plea to save James' life while Evelyn is pressured by her abusive boyfriend, Malcolm, to continue their charade of playing the "victims". Bobby and Shelly give their statement about Leo's rampage and disappearance, and also divulge that Hank Jennings that was the one who shot Leo on the night of the sawmill fire. Albert Rosenfield arrives in Twin Peaks to deliver to Cooper and Truman the classified file on the fugitive Windom Earle's motivations – "Springfield, Kansas City, Lawton, Dallas, Jackson" and "white veil, garter, white slippers, pearl necklace, white dress". At his cabin, the flute-playing Windom Earle holds the half-witted Leo against his will with an electric collar while he is forcibly recruited as Earle's henchman to help him stalk Cooper. Big Ed and Norma finally consummate their relationship, while Nadine finds out and reacts with indifference. Truman questions Josie about a murder (that of "Jonathan") back in Seattle. Cooper finally discovers that it was Josie who shot him at the Great Northern Hotel after finding a black vicuña coat in her dry-cleaning and finds unexpected help in Pete Martell in matching wits with Windom Earle in his deadly game of chess. Shelly asks for (and gets) her job back at the Double-R Diner. Catherine Martell dangles a helpless Josie Packard as booty before the eyes of an extremely dangerous man – the evil-hearted Thomas Eckhardt. Benjamin Horne changes the course of history at Appomattox while Audrey, Bobby, Jerry and Dr. Jacoby dress up in Civil War costumes to implement the 'Appomattox Scenario' to finally bring Ben back to reality. Evelyn kills Malcolm in a stand-off with Donna. Windom Earle leaves a nasty reminder for Cooper at the Great Northern Hotel. Unanswered Questions But WHY did Josie shoot Cooper? How will the Josie / Eckhardt situation resolve itself? What is Windom Earle's intention with Cooper? CAST LIST EPISODES CHARACTERS

title: 23 - The Condemned Woman | Twin Peaks
text: 23 - The Condemned Woman | Twin Peaks ← Previous Next → 23 - The Condemned Woman Written by Tricia Brock Directed by Lesli Linka Glatter Original Airdate: 16 February 1991 “ A hotel. A nightstand. A drawer pull on the drawer. A drawer pull of a nightstand in the room of a hotel. What could possibly be happening on or in this drawer pull? How many drawer pulls exist in this world? Thousands, maybe millions. “ What is a drawer pull? This drawer pull – why is it featured so prominently in a life or in a death of one woman who was caught in a web of power? Can a victim of power end in any way connected to a drawer pull? How can this be? ” Cooper and Truman try to outline the moves left by Windom Earle by investigating more of his past. Josie collapses when she sees Andrew Packard, whom she thought was dead, having breakfast with Catherine. Truman arrests Hank for parole violation and attempting to kill Leo, but Hank reveals that he and Josie were the ones who conspired to murder Andrew Packard. Audrey meets a potential new beau in the form of John Justice Wheeler, a business associate of the newly-sane Ben Horne, who comes to town to help thwart Catherine's development plans for Ghostwood Estates by holding a campaign to save the endangered Pine Weasel which resides on the development grounds. Windom Earle tears a poem (Shelley's Love's Philosophy ) into three and sends a piece each to Audrey, Donna and Shelly as a tantalising puzzle to the three women. Nadine admits to Ed that she is in love with Mike. Cooper pleads with Josie Packard for the truth as Catherine looks on. She says she escaped from Jonathan at the airport but didn't kill him. Shelly comes back to work at the Double-R Diner where she finds the message from Windom Earle. Ed Hurley proposes marriage to Norma Jennings who then visits Hank before he's sent back to prison to tell him that she wants a divorce. She refuses to give him an alibi regarding his shooting of Leo. Agent Rosenfeld leaves town but persuades Cooper to arrest Josie before she plans to escape. Donna finds herself saying goodbye to James who, although cleared of murder charges, tells her that he must follow his own path. Andrew Packard reveals that he's alive to both Josie and Thomas Eckhardt to try to bring them to kill each other as part of Catherine's evil plans. Catherine calls Cooper to warn him that Josie is heading for the Great Northern to kill Eckhardt. Cooper bursts into Eckhardt's room after hearing a gun shot. Eckhardt dies and, as Truman arrives, Josie dies of an apparent heart attack. Cooper has a vision of Killer BOB and The Man From Another Place while Josie's soul appears to be imprisoned in a drawer pull on the nightstand. Unanswered Questions What is WIndom Earle's plan for the three women? Why and how has Josie's soul been imprisoned? CAST LIST EPISODES CHARACTERS

title: 24 - Wounds And Scars | Twin Peaks
text: 24 - Wounds And Scars | Twin Peaks ← Previous Next → 24 - Wounds And Scars Written by Barry Pullman Directed by James Foley Original Airdate: 28 March 1991 “ Sometimes – well, let's say all times – things are changing. We are judged as human beings on how we treat our fellow human beings. How do you treat your fellow human beings? At night, just before sleep, as you lay by yourself in the dark, how do you feel about yourself? Are you proud of your behaviour? Are you ashamed of your behaviour? You know in your heart if you have hurt someone you know. If you have hurt someone, don't wait another day before making things right. The world could break apart with sadness in the meantime.” Truman is suffering from grief in the wake of Josie's unexplained death, and confines himself to the Bookhouse, drinking heavily. Norma's younger sister, Annie Blackburne, arrives in town and reveals that she has left the convent where she was living for the past five years since age 17, and claims that she is ready to face the world. Windom Earle reads in the newspaper of Cooper's latest chess moves, and becomes angry after immediately figuring out that Cooper is getting help. Meanwhile, Ben Horne plans to put on a charity event fashion show at the Great Northern in support of the endangered Pine Weasel, with financing from John Justice Wheeler and Dick Tremayne as the MC, who disdains help from Tim Pinkle. In the wake of Thomas Eckhardt's murder, his sinister Executive Assistant, Ms. Jones, puts his final plan of revenge into motion by delivering a mysterious box to Catherine. In disguise, Windom Earle individually contacts Donna (as "Dr. Gerald Craig") and Shelly (as a leather clad biker). Major Briggs and the Log Lady discover that they have similar mysterious markings on their bodies and alert Cooper to this fact. Both "disappeared" in the past and both have recollections of a flash of light and of owls screeching. Audrey continues flirting with Wheeler, while Andy tries to get back together with Lucy. Ed, through the intervention of Dr. Jacoby, breaks up with Nadine. Donna sees Ben Horne arrive at her house and kiss her mother in more than a platonic fashion. Norma encourages Shelly to enter the Miss Twin Peaks pageant. Cooper finds Norma's sister, Annie, very attractive but also notes the scar on her wrist. Cooper is forced to take over as temporary sheriff of Twin Peaks, and has Deputy Hawk help him follow more clues to Windom Earle's whereabouts. Mike Nelson and Nadine finally decide to consummate their growing romance by checking into the Great Northern Hotel as a married couple, although Mike is spotted by a school classmate. The fashion show descends into disaster when the Pine Weasel escapes and causes panic. Ms. Jones slips into bed with the comatose Sheriff Truman. Unanswered Questions What does Ms. Jones hope to achieve with her seduction of Sheriff Truman? What are Windom Earle's plans with his three female targets? CAST LIST EPISODES CHARACTERS

title: 25 - On The Wings Of Love | Twin Peaks
text: 25 - On The Wings Of Love | Twin Peaks ← Previous Next → 25 - On The Wings Of Love Written by Harley Peyton and Robert Engels Directed by Duwayne Dunham Original Airdate: 4 April 1991 “ The beautiful thing about treasure is that it exists. It exists to be found. How beautiful it is to find treasure. Where is the treasure that, when found, leaves one eternally happy? I think we all know it exists. Some say it is inside us – inside us one and all. That would be strange. It would be so near. Then why is it so hard to find, and so difficult to attain? ” Truman awakens in the murderous embrace of Ms. Jones but survives the attempt on his life and returns to his job. Truman is mystified as to why Thomas Eckhardt should want him dead. A bonsai tree has been delivered to the Sheriff's office. 'Doc' Hayward advises that Windom Earle had been at his house and left his next chess move with Donna. Gordon Cole returns to Twin Peaks to reinstate Cooper into the FBI and to bring the classified file on Windom Earle, who is now eavesdropping on the police station with a microphone which he has hidden in the bonsai tree. Donna Hayward enlists Audrey Horne's help in investigating Donna's mother who may have a past connection with Ben Horne. They witness a strange meeting between the two. When Cole flirts with Shelly at the Double-R Diner, her seductive appearance somehow makes him hear her voice. Enlightened that he can hear (her voice at least) Cole asks Shelly out on a date. Shelly is somewhat embarrassed but, flattered at the attention, accepts. Truman notes that Cooper and Annie Blackburne seem attracted to each other. When Annie sees the symbols that Cooper drew from descriptions from both Major Briggs and the Log Lady she tells them they look similar to markings in Owl Cave. Donna receives a postcard from the departed James Hurley in San Francisco on his way to Mexico, as well as an invitation to join the annual Miss Twin Peaks Beauty Pageant. Audrey continues pursuing Wheeler, but is thwarted by her father who sends her to Seattle on Pine Weasel ecology business. Windom Earle makes contact (in disguise as "Edward Perkins") with Audrey in the local library and reveals that the poem sent by Earle is by Shelley. Agent Cooper and the Sheriff's Department make a midnight trip to the cave where they discover mysterious petroglyph markings and are attacked by an owl. Andy retaliates and embeds his pick-axe in the rock face which exposes a further strange symbol. Over drinks at the Great Northern Hotel Cooper offers a hand of friendship to Annie Blackburne. Windom Earle makes his own way to Owl Cave and inverts the owl symbol, causing the rocks to shake alarmingly. Unanswered Questions What relevance do the petroglyph markings in Owl Cave have to the events in Twin Peaks? By inverting the owl symbol, what has Windom Earle unleashed? CAST LIST EPISODES CHARACTERS

title: 26 - Variations On Relations | Twin Peaks
text: 26 - Variations On Relations | Twin Peaks ← Previous Next → 26 - Variations On Relations Written by Mark Frost and Harley Peyton Directed by Jonathan Sanger Original Airdate: 11 April 1991 “ Pie. Whoever invented the pie? Here was a great person. In Twin Peaks, we specialise in cherry pie and huckleberry pie. We do have many other types of pies, and at the Double-R Diner, Norma knows how to make them all better than anyone I have ever known. I hope Norma likes me. I know I like her and respect her. I have spit my pitch gum out of my mouth onto her walls and floors and sometimes onto her booths. Sometimes I get angry and do things I'm not proud of. I do love Norma's pies. I love pie *with* coffee.” Cooper and Truman find the large map-like petroglyph discovered by Windom Earle in Owl Cave and try to unlock its secret. They enlist Major Briggs who agrees to help explain Windom Earle's role in Project Blue Book (the UFO investigation). Windom Earle picks up a heavy metal youth with the promise of beer to whom he confides his intentions to find the mysterious Black Lodge. Catherine shows Pete and Truman the mysterious puzzle box left behind by Thomas Eckhardt and, once opened, it reveals another box inside. As the town prepares for the Miss Twin Peaks Beauty Pageant, the conniving Lana Budding Milford enters as a contestant and persuades the elderly and senile Mayor Milford, who is one of the judges, to vote in her favour. Cooper learns about the love poem that Shelly, Donna and Audrey received from Windom Earle, and correctly concludes that Leo is also working for Earle. Dick Tremayne hosts a wine-tasting fund raiser at the Great Northern for Ben Horne's opposition to Catherine's development plans for Ghostwood. Leo begins to show disillusionment to Earle over his methods, but is held in check. Cooper continues dating Annie Blackburne, unaware that Windom Earle knows about their newfound romance. Gordon Cole goes on a date with Shelly and kisses her goodbye as he leaves Twin Peaks but is seen by Bobby. With Audrey out of town, Wheeler confides in Cooper about his feelings for Audrey, before receiving a telegram which causes him to check out of the Great Northern Hotel. Donna continues to investigate her parents’ past which may involve Ben Horne. A large crate is discovered in the town bandstand. When opened by Cooper it is found to contain the body of the heavy metal youth entombed in an elaborate, large, chess pawn. Unanswered Questions What will the map found in Owl Cave lead Cooper to discover? What will be Windom Earle's next chess move? CAST LIST EPISODES CHARACTERS

title: 27 - The Path To The Black Lodge | Twin Peaks
text: 27 - The Path To The Black Lodge | Twin Peaks ← Previous Next → 27 - The Path To The Black Lodge Written by Harley Peyton and Robert Engels Directed by Stephen Gyllenhaal Original Airdate: 19 April 1991 “ There are clues everywhere – all around us. But the puzzle maker is clever. The clues, although surrounding us, are somehow mistaken for something else. And the something else – the *wrong* interpretation of the clues – we call our world. Our world is a magical smoke screen. How should we interpret the happy song of the meadowlark or the robust flavour of a wild strawberry? ” Cooper and Truman try to figure out Windom Earle's next move following the discovery of the heavy metal youth's body in a large chess pawn. Lucy decides to enter the Miss Twin Peaks Beauty Pageant as the prize money would be useful for the unborn baby. She tells Andy that she will choose who the father of the baby will be in 24 hours. Wheeler searches for Audrey before he has to leave town for Brazil to take over his murdered partner's business, and leaves a letter for Audrey. Ben Horne has a health check up from 'Doc' Hayward who warns him to stay away from his wife. Ben is determined to "do the right thing". Donna Hayward finds an old scrapbook full of surprises including her birth certificate on which her father's name is not included. Cooper and Truman continue to investigate the mystery of Owl Cave and learn from Major Briggs that Windom Earle's real reason for being in Twin Peaks is to gain entrance into the Black Lodge. Cooper realises that the "chess game" has been a "red herring". Cooper contacts Donna, Shelly and Audrey and confides about Windom Earle and warns them to be careful; however the lovesick Cooper does not think about warning Annie who also decides to enter the Beauty Pageant. Lana continues her plans to fix the beauty pageant in her favour. Major Briggs is abducted by Earle and Leo who interrogate him for information to what the Owl Cave markings mean, and learn that they are an actual map to the Black Lodge. Audrey gets Pete, who is still mourning the loss of Josie, to rush her to the airport to intercept Wheeler to whom she makes a major confession. Catherine shows Andrew Packard the puzzle box, who manages to get it open to reveal a small silver box. Cooper dances with Annie and has a vision of The Giant who appears to be mouthing the word "No". In a clearing in the woods, BOB appears. Unanswered Questions How will Windom Earle find the Black Lodge now that he has the map? What does The Giant's warning mean? CAST LIST EPISODES CHARACTERS

title: 28 - Miss Twin Peaks | Twin Peaks
text: 28 - Miss Twin Peaks | Twin Peaks ← Previous Next → 28 - Miss Twin Peaks Written by Barry Pullman Directed by Tim Hunter Original Airdate: 10 June 1991 (Holding log directly in front of her, instead of the usual position cradled in her arms.) “ A log is a portion of a tree. (Turning end of log to camera.) “ At the end of a crosscut log – many of you know this – there are rings. Each ring represents one year in the life of the tree. How long it takes to a grow a tree! I don't mind telling you some things. Many things I mustn't say. Just notice that my fireplace is boarded up. (She glances over her right shoulder at the fireplace and the camera moves over to it, where we see the opening covered by plywood.) “ There will never be a fire there. (Camera pans up to the mantel where we see a vase, a pipe stand, and some old pictures – none recognizable.) “ On the mantelpiece, in that jar, are some of the ashes of my husband. (Camera pans back down to Log Lady.) “ My log hears things I cannot hear. But my log tells me about the sounds, about the new words. Even though it has stopped growing larger, my log is aware.” Windom Earle has handcuffed both Leo and Major Briggs. Leo manages to release the Major with a plea to "save Shelly". A hideously ashen Windom Earle discovers and retaliates by tying Leo to a lethal device and leaves both the cabin and Leo to an uncertain fate. Norma looks forward to the Miss Twin Peaks Beauty Pageant as a way to move forward after Laura Palmer's death and it is revealed that Norma was a previous winner of the Pageant. Ben continues to seek a path to goodness, while Audrey confides that she is missing Wheeler but also that her business trip to Seattle has revealed that the Twin Peaks Savings & Loan is supporting Catherine's development plans for Ghostwood. Cooper confides to Truman that, at the time of Josie's death she was "quaking like an animal" and, as she died, Cooper saw BOB who seemed to be drawn by her fear. Cooper believes there is a connection between BOB's appearance and the Black Lodge – previously described by Truman as "the evil in these woods". All this is overheard by Windom Earle via the bonsai tree. Mr. Pinkle rehearses dance moves with the other contestants while Lana seduces Dick Tremayne to get him to vote for her in the Beauty Pageant. Cooper and Annie consummate their relationship after she calls round to his hotel room to ask for help with her Beauty Pageant speech. Nadine reveals to Dr. Jacoby that she wants to marry Mike Nelson as soon as Big Ed and Norma are married. The delusional and dehydrated Major Briggs is found by Deputy Hawk and returned to the police station where he makes little sense about his captivity, but leaves clues to how to find the Black Lodge. Andy discovers that the cave painting is a map to the lodge itself but finds it difficult to pass this information to Cooper. Andrew and Pete manage to get the last silver box open to reveal a safety deposit key. Donna finally learns the secret from Ben Horne about him and her mother – Ben is actually her biological father. Lucy finally chooses Andy to be the father for her baby. The Beauty Pageant gets underway as Windom Earle arrives at the event disguised as the Log Lady intending to abduct Annie. Unanswered Questions Where will Windom Earle take Annie? As Andy realises the cave painting is a map, can he use it to find the Black Lodge entrance? CAST LIST EPISODES CHARACTERS

title: 29 - Beyond Life and Death | Twin Peaks
text: 29 - Beyond Life and Death | Twin Peaks ← Previous Next → 29 - Beyond Life And Death Written by Mark Frost, Harley Peyton and Robert Engels Directed by David Lynch Original Airdate: 10 June 1991 " And now, an ending. Where there was once one, there are now two. Or were there always two? " What is a reflection? A chance to see two? When there are chances for reflections, there can always be two - or more. Only when we are everywhere will there be just one. It has been a pleasure speaking to you. " (Throughout the above, the camera has been slowing zooming in until only the Log Lady's face is framed. As she finishes speaking, the camera continues to zoom in. As it gets closer and closer, the Log Lady looks nervously up, down, and to her left, before staring straight ahead as the camera moves in through her left (our right) glass frame. As the iris of her left eye fills the screen, the screen turns completely white, then we hear a hissing sound, and then a 'door slamming' sound as the screen turns from white to black.) In the series final, Cooper faces his innermost fears as he tracks down Windom Earle, who has abducted Annie, and takes her into the hellish realm of the Black Lodge. Lucy and Andy celebrate the fact that they are back together and escaped the confusion at the Pageant. They declare their love for each other. Pete bursts into the Sheriff's office stating that the Log Lady has stolen his pick-up truck and taken it to the woods. Cooper says it was not the Log Lady but Windom Earle in disguise. Truman realises that there is a circle of 12 sycamore trees in the woods known as Glastonbury Grove. Hawk says this is where he found the bloody towel and pages of the diary. The Log Lady arrives with a jar of oil which her husband brought back just before he died and said "This oil is an opening to a gateway". It smells of scorched engine oil. The jar of oil is shown to Ronette Pulaski who smells it and is terrified. It reminds her of the night Laura Palmer was killed. Nadine, wounded by a hit on the head during the beauty pageant, wakes up now back to her old self, and is devastated when she sees Big Ed with Norma. Donna struggles to control herself from Ben Horne's news, which leads to a fist fight between him and 'Doc' Hayward who angrily knocks Ben into a fireplace mantle for interfering with his family, apparently killing him. Andrew Packard steals the safety deposit box key from its place under the cake stand in Catherine's house. Cooper and Truman find Pete's pick-up truck and Glastonbury Grove. Cooper follows Annie and Earle into the Lodge, which turns out to be the red-curtained room from his dream; he is greeted by the Man From Another Place, the Night Service Waiter, the Giant and the spirit of Laura Palmer who each give Cooper encoded prophecies about his future and demonstrate the properties of the Black Lodge, which defy the laws of time and space. Andrew Packard and Pete take the safety deposit box key and go to the Twin Peaks Savings & Loan where Audrey is staging a feeble act of civil disobedience using the feeble-minded Dell Mibbler. When Andrew and Pete open Thomas Eckhardt's deposit box, they instead find a bomb ... which explodes. Bobby Briggs proposes marriage to Shelly, but she is aware she is still wearing Leo's ring. Major Briggs receives a cryptic message from Windom Earle in the Black Lodge through the conduit of Sarah Palmer. In the Black Lodge, Cooper encounters doppelgängers of various dead people, including Maddy, Caroline / Annie and Leland Palmer, who taunt him with strange, false statements; the doppelgängers eventually lead Cooper to Earle, who demands that Cooper give up his soul in exchange for Annie's life; Cooper agrees and Earle kills him. Killer BOB appears and reverses time in the Lodge, bringing Cooper back to life; BOB tells Earle that he cannot take human souls and then kills Earle and takes his soul; BOB then turns on Cooper, who for the first time in the Lodge, experiences fear; Cooper flees, pursued by BOB and a laughing doppelgänger of himself. Days after entering the Lodge, Cooper and Annie are discovered in the woods by Sheriff Truman; Annie is hospitalized, but Cooper's injuries are minor enough that 'Doc' Hayward is able to treat them in Cooper's room at the Great Northern Hotel. Upon waking, Cooper asks about Annie's condition, and then states he needs to brush his teeth; when Cooper enters the bathroom and looks into the mirror, his reflection reveals that he is now inhabited by BOB; he then rams his face into the mirror and while laughing, rhetorically continues asking about Annie's condition, ending the series with an unresolved cliffhanger.
